transcript.text: My Beko keeps stopping randomly in the middle of a wash with water still in it. Sometimes it's fine for a week, then it does it twice in a day. The model starts WTG I think. I've cleaned the filter. Driving me mad.

That stop-start pattern is maddening, but it does narrow things down. A machine that stalls with water in the drum is usually doing one of two things. Either it can't empty properly and gives up, or it is losing power, losing the door lock, or hitting a control glitch partway through. Less often, it is stuck waiting to reach temperature because of a heating or temperature-sensor fault. A full blockage there is less likely. A partial blockage further along, or a pump that sticks now and then, is still possible. 1. If the display goes completely dead, or the lights reset, that points to power. Check the plug and socket for looseness or warmth. Also avoid running it on an extension lead or adaptor, as these commonly cause random cut-outs.
2. If the display stays on and shows a code or flashing lights, note exactly what it shows. On a Beko, a code usually points straight at drain, door lock or heating.
3. If it's paused just before it should drain or spin, it's most likely a drain problem. Two quick things are worth doing meanwhile. Switch off and unplug first.
1. Pull the machine out a little and check the drain hose isn't kinked or squashed behind it. Also check it isn't pushed too far down the standpipe, which can cause siphoning and confuse the machine.
2. If you use a lot of detergent, cut back. Excess foam can make it pause or refuse to spin. It's worth jotting down the full number, as it helps if a part turns out to be needed. So, when it next stops: is the display still lit, does it show a code, and what stage is it at?

Right, so when it stops the display just freezes, the time stops counting down, and sometimes there's a flashing light I think is the start button. No proper code that I can tell. Hose is fine, goes into a standpipe, and I use a measured pod so no foam. Sometimes if I switch it off and on it carries on, other times it stalls again.

That's really useful, and it shifts things away from draining. The display stays on, the timer freezes, there's no code and switching off and on sometimes gets it going again. That pattern says the machine is pausing because it's waiting for something, not because it has lost power or given up draining. On Beko machines a flashing Start light usually means the programme is paused, often because it has stopped seeing the door as locked. The two likeliest causes, in order:
1. The door lock (interlock) intermittently losing its 'locked' signal. The machine pauses for safety, and a restart sometimes lets it re-lock. This fits the flashing Start light best.
2. A heating fault. On many machines the timer stops while the programme waits to reach temperature. A failing heater element or temperature sensor can do this on and off. If so, the stalls would be on warmer washes, partway through the wash rather than near the end. The next time it stops, before switching off, try these:
1. Press Start once. If you hear the lock click and it carries on, that points to the door lock or its connection. If it does nothing and just sits there, it's more likely waiting for something else, such as temperature.
2. Note the programme and temperature. If it only ever stalls on 40°C or hotter, and the door glass feels cool even though it's well into the wash, that points to heating. If it also stalls on 20 or 30°C washes, heating becomes much less likely.
3. Note roughly how far into the programme it is, for example 15 minutes in or near the end, and whether the drum is still turning now and then. One quick thing meanwhile: open the door, check nothing is caught in the seal, then close it firmly until it clicks. If the door drops slightly on its hinge or the catch looks worn, that can cause exactly this kind of on-off lock signal. If the checks don't separate it, an engineer can test the door lock and heating circuit directly. The control board is the last thing to suspect here, not the first. So, which temperature programme is it on when it stalls, and does pressing Start make it click and carry on?

It's stalled on cold ones too, so not just hot washes. I haven't tried pressing Start when it stops, I'll try that next time. Also checked the door seal, nothing caught in it that I can see. Anything else worth looking at?

It makes a heating fault much less likely, because on a cold wash the machine isn't waiting for any temperature. That leaves the door lock as the front runner. A wiring or connection problem to the lock, or a control glitch, comes second. A false water-level reading is an outside chance. 1. Check the catch and hinge. Switch off and unplug first. Look at the small hook on the door and the slot it goes into. Is the hook bent, cracked or worn shiny on one side? Close the door slowly and see whether the hook lines up squarely with the slot. Lift the open door gently by its edge. More than a little up-and-down play means the hinge has dropped. Either of these can give exactly this on-off lock signal.
2. Next time it stalls, before you switch off, press Start once and listen for a click. If nothing happens, press firmly on the door near the handle, or lift it slightly, and press Start again. If it resumes when you push or lift the door, the hinge or catch alignment is the cause. If it clicks and carries on without touching the door, the lock itself is the likeliest part. It can also be its connection.
3. While it's stalled, glance through the glass. Note whether the water level looks about normal (covering the bottom of the door) or unusually high or low. A clearly odd level would point towards the water-level sensing instead.
4. Rule out the simple one. A flashing Start light can also mean the programme has been paused. Make sure nobody is brushing the Start/Pause button, and check a knob isn't being knocked between programmes. If the catch and hinge look fine and pressing Start gets it going, the most likely part is the door interlock. Because the fault is intermittent, an engineer can confirm it by testing the lock and its wiring before anything is replaced. The control board is very much last on the list. So, when it next stops: does pressing Start make it click and carry on, and does pushing or lifting the door change anything?

Ok, I'll try the Start button and the door push next time it stalls. I'm not taking the machine apart though, so I can't check anything inside. Is there anything else I should note down when it happens?

Yes, a few more observations would help a lot, and none of them need anything opened up. 1. How far into the programme it is. Is it early on (filling or washing), mid-rinse, or just before a spin? Stalls always at the same stage point one way. Stalls at random points fit the door lock.
2. Whether the drum is still or turning now and then, and what you hear. Is it silent, humming, or can you hear water hissing in or the pump running? Water still trickling in suggests it's waiting on a slow fill. Note whether someone was running a shower or tap elsewhere at the time. Silence with the drum still fits the lock signal dropping out.
3. Any lock or key symbol on the display, or a door light. Does it go out or flash when it stalls? That would point firmly at the door lock.
4. The Start button test and the door push you're already planning. Note whether you heard the lock click.
5. The programme and load size each time. A pattern, such as only on heavy loads, can matter.
6. Take a quick photo or short video of the display when it's stuck. An engineer will find that genuinely useful. Please don't try to force the door open while it's stalled with water in it. It's just looking and gently lifting the open door, nothing taken apart. If your notes show the lock symbol dropping out, or a push on the door brings it back to life, the door interlock or the door alignment is the likely culprit. An engineer can confirm which by testing the lock and its wiring. The full model number from the sticker round the door rim would help at that point too.
